title: In 1917, One Ship Exploded and Killed Nearly 2,000 People

scenes.text: In 1917, one ship exploded and killed nearly 2,000 people.
Two ships collided in Halifax harbour. One was packed with high explosives.
Twenty minutes later it went off. The biggest man made explosion before the atomic bomb.
Five thousand degrees. A half tonne chunk of anchor flew two miles. The harbour rose in a 59 foot wave.
Nine thousand injured. Hundreds blinded, because they'd run to the windows to watch the fire.
The next morning, a blizzard buried the ruins in 16 inches of snow.

description:
On December 6, 1917, the munitions ship Mont-Blanc collided with another vessel in Halifax harbour, Canada, caught fire and exploded about twenty minutes later.
The blast, roughly 2.9 kilotons, was the largest man-made explosion before the atomic bomb. It reached about 5,000 degrees Celsius, threw a half-tonne piece of the anchor two miles, raised a tsunami up to 59 feet and killed nearly 2,000 people; around 9,000 were injured and hundreds were blinded by window glass. A blizzard hit the next day.
Had you ever heard of the Halifax Explosion? Comment below.
first_comment: Boston sent doctors and supplies by train within hours. Every year since 1971, Nova Scotia has thanked Boston with a giant Christmas tree for Boston Common. What's a historical disaster you think more people should know about?
